1. Nonstandard threat to describe user specific conditions  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:User-defined
Description:
Justification:This threat is mitigated through Host Hardening and Docker Container Isolation. The host machine (DESKTOP-8TCFF7Q\HP) is secured by a firewall that blocks all ports except those strictly necessary for the application. To prevent a &#39;container breakout&#39; where an attacker could take control of the host, the application and database run as non-root users within Docker. We have also disabled Docker&#39;s default bridge network in favor of a custom private network, ensuring that services are not exposed to the local host network unnecessarily. This is verified by Secret Scanning to ensure no host SSH keys are leaked and Snyk to audit the container base images for OS-level vulnerabilities

Interaction: Request

2. Weakness in SSO Authorization  [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Elevation Of Privilege
Description:This threat is mitigated by enforcing PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for the OAuth2 flow and requiring mandatory HTTPS (TLS 1.2+) for all token exchanges. This prevents authorization code injection and interception. We also use Short-lived Access Tokens and Rotation of Refresh Tokens to limit the window of opportunity for an attacker. Additionally, the system implements Strict Redirect URI Validation to prevent token leakage to malicious domains. This is verified using DAST (OWASP ZAP) to check for protocol vulnerabilities and Snyk (SCA) to ensure the SSO libraries used are up to date and free of known vulnerabilities like 'Covert Redirect
Justification:<no mitigation provided>

Interaction: Request

4. Spoofing of Source Data Store Payment gateway   [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Spoofing
Description:This threat is mitigated by implementing Webhook Signature Verification. Every response sent from the Payment Gateway to Cart Management is digitally signed using a secret key. Our system recalculates the HMAC signature and compares it with the one provided in the header to ensure the data is coming from the authentic provider. Additionally, we use IP Whitelisting to only accept requests from known Payment Gateway IP ranges, which is verified during DAST testing.
Justification:<no mitigation provided>

18. Potential Excessive Resource Consumption for Host or Order Database   [State: Mitigation Implemented]  [Priority: High] 

Category:Denial Of Service

Additionally, an API Gateway enforces Rate Limiting (requests per second) to block volumetric Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. These controls are verified through Load Testing and Chaos Engineering to ensure system stability under stress.
